fields.subject: IMPORTANT PRESCRIBING AND ADMINISTRATION INFORMATION — Temporary Importation of 0.9% Sodium Chloride Intravenous Infusion, 500 mL, Lot IMP-2609-114, Exp 08/2028 [EXERCISE PRODUCT — NOT A REAL FDA DOCUMENT]
fields.body:
To help with the current U.S. shortage of 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection, Northbridge Medical Import Services is distributing 0.9% Sodium Chloride Intravenous Infusion, 500 mL, which was made for a market outside the United States. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration does not object to its temporary importation while the shortage lasts. This shipment is from Lot IMP-2609-114, expiration 08/2028. The product is not FDA-approved in this presentation. Please make sure everyone who stocks, prepares, programs or gives it understands the differences below.

Label and product differences: (1) The primary bag label is not in English. Use the English translation on the enclosed comparison table. (2) The bag volume is 500 mL. The U.S. product it replaces is 1000 mL. (3) The concentration is 9 mg/mL, the same as U.S. 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection. (4) The bag has a twist-off administration port that needs a vented spike set. Do not use a non-vented set. (5) The bag has no U.S. barcode, so it will not scan in pharmacy or bedside barcode systems.

Infusion pump programming: when you program an infusion pump, enter the volume to be infused as the volume of the bag actually hung (500 mL), not the 1000 mL volume of the U.S. product. Facilities should check whether the product is compatible with their own pump drug libraries and administration sets before use.

To report adverse events or product quality problems, or for medical information, call Northbridge Medical Information at (502) 555-0163. Facilities may also report to FDA MedWatch.

instructorNote: This tests whether the CPM keeps the imported bags in pharmacy until the full PH-22-A section 3 checklist is complete (Prairie Ridge label, nursing alert, second pharmacist check), whether the PIM tracks down and recalls the 2 missing cases by lot, and whether the CNO keeps the bags off units until nurses are briefed. After handing over the letter, read aloud the Clinical Informatics email ("Can't add it to Thursday 02:00's push. Cutoff was Tuesday noon. Earliest is an off-cycle build Friday night, pending biomed. Until then it's basic mode with no library limits on all 240 pumps.") and storeroom technician's report ("Two cases are already missing from the dock pallet. A float nurse said the ICU satellite 'needed them' and signed the packing slip.").
